source_text:
Fragmenta in Joannem
Jo , 3 Ἐν τούτῳ δὲ ἀνέτρεπεν αὐτὸς ὁ σωτὴρ δόγμα παράνομον.
ὑπονοούντων γάρ τινων ψυχὰς ἁμαρτανούσας ἐξ οὐρανοῦ τιμωρίας ἕνεκεν εἰς σῶμα
πέμπεσθαι καί ποτε μὲν καθ' ἑαυτὴν προϋπάρχουσαν τὴν ψυχὴν τοῦ σώματος
<μένειν>, ποτὲ δὲ οἰκείων ἁμαρτημάτων χάριν σώμασι συμπλέκεσθαι καὶ τότε κατὰ
γαστρὸς ἔχειν τὴν γυναῖκα δύνασθαι ὅτε τις ψυχὴ ἁμαρτάνῃ, ἀναιρῶν τὴν τοιαύτην
πλάνην ἐρωτηθεὶς ὁ Χριστὸς ἔλεγεν· οὔτε οὗτος ἥμαρτεν οὔτε οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ, ἀλλ'
ἵνα φανερωθῇ τὰ ἔργα θεοῦ.

1
thought_title: Christ overturns the unlawful doctrine of souls sent into bodies
orientation: The author introduces a fragment on John 3, explaining that Christ himself overturned an unlawful doctrine held by some about souls being sent into bodies for punishment.
pass_a_gloss: And in this the Savior himself was overturning an unlawful doctrine. For since some supposed that sinning souls are sent from heaven into a body for the sake of punishment, and that sometimes the soul pre-exists by itself and remains apart from the body, but sometimes it is intertwined with bodies on account of its own sins, and that then the woman is able to conceive whenever some soul sins, destroying such error, Christ, having been asked, said: neither this one sinned nor his parents, but that the works of God might be revealed.

choices.why: The glossary mandates this rendering for the fixed term, avoiding 'illegal dogma' or 'lawless teaching'.
Keeps the participle active and the noun 'souls' as the glossary requires, preserving the opponents' claim that souls themselves sin.
Renders the purpose clause literally, keeping 'punishment' as the glossary term and the causal force of ἕνεκεν.
The glossary mandates 'pre-existing' for this term, and the participle is kept as an adjective modifying 'soul'.
The glossary mandates 'error' for this term, avoiding 'deception' or 'delusion'.
The glossary mandates this exact rendering for the fixed phrase.

bible_refs.note: The quotation 'οὔτε οὗτος ἥμαρτεν οὔτε οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ, ἀλλ' ἵνα φανερωθῇ τὰ ἔργα θεοῦ' closely matches John 9:3, though the manuscript marks the passage as John 3.

pass_b_english: In this, the Savior himself was overturning an unlawful doctrine. For some people supposed that sinning souls are sent from heaven into a body for the sake of punishment, and that sometimes the soul remains pre-existing by itself apart from the body, while at other times it is intertwined with bodies on account of its own sins—so that a woman can conceive only when some soul sins. Destroying this error, Christ, when he was asked, said: "Neither this man sinned nor his parents, but this happened so that the works of God might be revealed" (John 3).
notes: The source marks the citation as 'Jo , 3' (John 3), but the quoted words resemble John 9:3. The manuscript attribution must be respected, with possible textual variation or conflation.

problems.why: Source marks citation as John 3; modern citation must respect manuscript attribution.
problems.fix: (John 3), with note that the words resemble John 9:3

last_rejected.quote: remains pre-existing by itself apart from the body
last_rejected.source_quote: ποτε μὲν καθ' ἑαυτὴν προϋπάρχουσαν τὴν ψυχὴν τοῦ σώματος <μένειν>
last_rejected.why: Greek says soul pre-exists body, not 'remains pre-existing apart from body'; μένειν is editorial supplement.
last_rejected.fix: sometimes the soul pre-exists by itself before the body
last_rejected.ruling: καθ' ἑαυτὴν means 'by itself'; pre-existing apart from body fits the context of souls existing separately before embodiment.

last_rejected.source_quote: ἀλλ' ἵνα φανερωθῇ τὰ ἔργα θεοῦ
last_rejected.why: English adds 'this happened' not in source; Christ says 'but that the works of God might be revealed'.
last_rejected.fix: but that the works of God might be revealed
last_rejected.ruling: ἵνα with finite verb naturally renders 'so that'; 'this happened' is implicit bridging, not a meaning-changing addition.
